messages:
tanya: flagging something odd from the ruby sample-app onboarding e2e. at TRACE level we see API keys in the logs. i thought our redactor handled that across languages. repro below.

sam: whoa that's bad. TRACE is noisy but still shouldn't log secrets. can you paste the snippet?

rohan: minimal repro steps from tanya: 
```bash
RAILS_ENV=development LOG_LEVEL=trace bin/rails server -p 4000
curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/api/v1/onboard -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"u@example.com"}'
```
log output: 
```
I, [2025-11-12T14:22:11.123456 #3456] TRACE -- : onboarding_controller#create params={"user"=>{"email"=>"u@example.com", "api_key"=>"sk_live_abcdef123456"}}
```
no obfuscated token.

marta: looks like the Rails logger is serializing the params before our rack middleware redactor runs. middleware sees the request body but not the params object after Rails has parsed it and logged it. our redactor currently hooks into the Rack request phase only.

sam: is this a difference between structured (otel) logs and Rails default string logs? iirc OTEL exporter goes through our SDK serializer where redaction runs, but plain logger calls skip it.

rohan: yes. root cause: redaction is only applied inside the SDK's json_encoder path. languages that funnel through that (node/python) get covered more often. ruby sample uses default Rails logger calls in controllers which bypass the encoder. TRACE mags are especially bad because controllers dump full params.

tanya: quick mitigation for sample-apps: add a global ActiveSupport::LogSubscriber patch that filters out api_key/api_token keys before the logger formats the message. but for the SDK we should fix the core: move redaction earlier to an IO-level wrapper so everything passing through the logger (structured or not) is scrubbed.

marta: proposals: 
- short term: monkeypatch rails logger in sample app + a conspicuous quickstart note about TRACE risks
- medium term: implement logger IO wrapper (redactor_io) in ruby SDK that sanitizes strings for known patterns and sensitive param keys
- long term: add a pre-log hook into our cross-language logging contract so any host logger sees the redactor first (prefer this).

sam: also worth adding a CI-housekeeping check: run integration e2e with LOG_LEVEL=trace and grep logs for sk_live_|sk_test_ and fail build if found. better safe than sorry.

rohan: agreed. i'll open a ticket and include a small patch for the sample app and CI check. created DEVEX-4001: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DEVEX-4001 (ruby redaction: ensure io-level scrub for logger). assigning @rohan to lead.

devex-bot: created DEVEX-4001 and added reviewers @marta @sam. :file_folder:

ci-bot: note: branch redaction/ruby-iowrap pushed; build #2030.5.12-42 started. failing tests expected until patch lands. :building_construction:

tanya: thanks team. i'll also update the ruby quickstart with a warning about TRACE and an example of setting config.log_level = :debug for dev. let's keep TRACE reserved for local debug only and make sure samples never print secrets at any level by default. :lock:
